A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HoPE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete included appendices support comparison: Appendices A-C in v1 and A-D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, language-model evaluations, copying and few-shot experiments, ablations, and scaling studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original small-model experiments and adds 3B-model benchmark results, training-progress evaluations, and a HoPE attention-pattern analysis.

M1.justification: HoPE retains the same frequency cutoff and procedure: rotate high-frequency components while making selected lower-frequency components position-independent. Equations 6-7 remain substantively equivalent; notation edits and larger experimental models do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on MMLU, MMLU-PRO, GPQA, BBH, WinoGrande, GSM8k, MATH, and DROP, substantially extending coverage to knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, and reading comprehension. RedPajama, C4, copying, and the existing three GLUE-based following tasks remain. The new GLUE breakdown does not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: The retained 125M comparisons preserve their comparator sets. However, v1's 300M scaling study compares ALiBi, KERPLE, FIRE, RoPE, and PI/YaRN variants, whereas its replacement in v2 evaluates the 3B model against RoPE alone. Baseline breadth therefore narrows in the scalability evidence, under different experimental settings.

E3.justification: v2 introduces 3B training with an 8192-token context, 120,000 updates, approximately 500B processed tokens, and benchmark-specific shot counts. The 300M experiments and HoPE training-length sweep are removed. Appendix A also changes the 125M batch-size entry from 32 × 8 to 64 × 8, resolving a discrepancy with v1's prose without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct HoPE-versus-RoPE attention analysis within and beyond training length (Section 4.3, Figure 5), plus benchmark trajectories over training (Appendix D, Figure 9). It removes v1's controlled model-size and training-length scaling analyses. The three component ablations and the 1024-token RoPE analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark results. Figure 1's shaded attention bands already appear in v1; v2 introduces no defined uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports 3B averages of 24.23 for RoPE and 26.42 for HoPE, with HoPE higher on seven benchmarks but lower on WinoGrande (50.43 versus 51.70). Appendix C.2 adds per-task following results and Appendix D adds checkpoint results. The 300M and longer-training-length results disappear. Matched 125M copying, following, and ablation tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The rotation matrices, attention decomposition, VAF formula, and HoPE cutoff and attention equations remain substantively unchanged. Relocated background equations and component/index notation edits introduce no new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit claim of better performance on complex NLP tasks using 3B models, extending v1's emphasis on context awareness and extrapolation experiments. The three stated contributions and central claim against long-term decay remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 interprets HoPE's milder positional fluctuations as potentially favoring semantic information and its lack of RoPE-like OOD behavior as explaining extrapolation benefits. v1's scaling-specific interpretations disappear. The shortcut-learning explanation and cautions about perplexity remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds 3B architecture and hardware details, including 34 layers and 256 A100 GPUs, and supplies layer counts. v2 also identifies OpenCompass and clarifies averaging attention over layers and heads. Earlier 300M configurations, dropout entries, and the explicit 2000-step VAF sampling interval are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting RAG motivation, new benchmarks, and Llama/Qwen evaluation conventions while retaining the positional-encoding research positioning. Its new OpenCompass citation to Fu et al. (2024) internally mismatches the bibliography, which lists a GET transcription-model paper.

P1.justification: RoPE background moves into Related Work, general settings become part of the attention-analysis section, and task terminology changes to in-context copying and few-shot following. Local prose and grammar are revised, but much of the introduction, method, ablation discussion, and conclusion remains closely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the prominent first-page benchmark table, HoPE attention comparison, full-width task-breakdown table, and eight-panel training-progress figure, while removing the earlier scaling displays. Figures 2, 6, and 7 are redrawn with grouped component colors, revised legends and axes; Figure 2's panels are reordered.

improvement.justification: The 3B benchmarks strengthen practical validation beyond v1's small-model evidence, while the direct HoPE attention comparison and previously missing per-task breakdown improve support and transparency. However, v2 removes controlled model-size and training-length studies, supplies no dedicated 3B extrapolation test, and introduces an incorrect OpenCompass reference. These tradeoffs leave a supported but limited net improvement.
